html:
In April 1652 Jan van Riebeeck landed at Table Bay with about ninety people to set up a supply station for the Dutch East India Company (VOC). It was the start of European settlement in South Africa.

The Cape lay halfway between the Netherlands and the company's trading posts in Asia. Since Dias rounded the Cape in 1488 ships had stopped there for water. Van Riebeeck built a fort and planted gardens to sell fresh food and meat to passing fleets.

The station soon grew into a colony. In 1657 some company men were freed to farm for themselves. From 1658 enslaved people were brought from Asia and other parts of Africa. Farmers spread inland onto the grazing land of the Khoekhoe, and the first war with them broke out in 1659. French Huguenots arrived in 1688. The colony stayed Dutch until Britain took it in 1795 and again in 1806, and it became the Cape Colony.
sum: In April 1652 Jan van Riebeeck landed at Table Bay with about ninety people to set up a supply station for the Dutch East India Company (VOC). It was the start of European settlement in South Africa.
